ancillary_coverage.alpaca_cross_check: Alpaca cash-dividend amounts are compared with the issuer's on shared ex-dates at 6 decimal places; matches, mismatches and ex-dates missing from either side are recorded and never gate.
ancillary_coverage.corporate_actions: One all-types SPY request, process_date filtered from anchor-31d to last+31d (default data_quality=complete). Actions are placed by their documented ex_date or effective_date, never by process_date. r9 keeps the r8 automatic stop on an in-window SPY split and the unsupported-valuation stop for other non-cash SPY actions. The whole response must still pass the schema, because the same pages carry the split stop: a malformed record of any group (for example a dividend with a null rate) ends the study UNRESOLVED (data). Only Alpaca cash-distribution values are non-gating: they feed no valuation and are compared with the issuer schedule as a cross-check. A same-ticker name change (old and new symbol both SPY) changes no valuation and is counted as non-gating metadata.
ancillary_coverage.dividend_quarter_presence: Every window quarter must show an issuer cash-dividend ex-date (SPY pays quarterly per its issuer). This is a conservative coverage sanity check on the issuer schedule only.
ancillary_coverage.exclusions: R1 (r9 protocol section 3): 2019-08-12 and 2019-08-13 are removed from the scored series, not counted as flat days, because their required price bars do not exist in the data (2019-08-12 lacks the 15:30 entry bar and the 15:59 exit bar; 2019-08-13 consequently lacks its prior-close anchor). The list was chosen after the missing timestamps were known but before any price, signal or return was seen. Losing a day for a reason linked to how the market moved that day could bias the result; that effect cannot be measured without prices, so it is a named limitation.
ancillary_coverage.issuer_distribution_schedule: Every SPY cash distribution comes from State Street's SPDR historical-distribution workbook, refused unless its SHA256 equals ISSUER_WORKBOOK_SHA256. Rows are identified by ticker SPY and CUSIP 78462F103; each needs one parseable ex-date (an official calendar session inside the window), a positive per-share dividend and, when a capital-gain field is filled, a non-negative finite value; a blank capital-gain field is no data, never zero, and a filled 0.000000 capital-gain leg is accepted (the workbook has such legs in window; r9's positive-amount check is read as applying to the dividend). Row checks run on every SPY row in the pinned workbook, including rows before the window. Per-ex-date payouts feed only the SPY total-return comparison and the ex-dividend-flat sensitivity; the rule's returns use raw prices.
limitations: Alpaca documents no guarantee on corporate-action creation or processing delay, so the 31-day process_date margin is not a completeness bound.
Quarter presence cannot prove that every historical action was returned; an absent split in the response is not certified absence.
Vendor adjustment changes have no machine-readable feed. The review record is a bounded human documentation review; it does not prove that no undocumented change exists.
The issuer workbook is a hash-pinned copy of one published file; it is not an audit of the issuer's records. Its amounts are assumed USD per share (the column is labelled DIVIDEND ($)).
ancillary_coverage.vendor_adjustment_review: Collection, PASS and scoring require the hash-bound local r9 review record at VENDOR_REVIEW_PATH (status reviewed, SPY, window and r9 protocol hash bound, no known unresolved changes); its SHA256 is in the manifest and the validation identities.
